column3: “Laughed on me” is rendered “mock me,” and “young more than me to days” as “younger than I.” “Rejected” is rendered “disdained.”
“What … to me on them” is rendered “what good was … to me.”
“Barren” is rendered “gaunt,” and “yesterday” as “by night”; the meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB supplies “as against.”
“On the slope of wadis” is rendered “in dreadful valleys”; the meaning is uncertain.
“Bray” is rendered “cry out.”
“Sons of a fool also sons of not a name” is rendered “Fools, even those without a name.”
“A word” is rendered “a byword.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The written text reads “his string,” the reading aloud “my string”; NASB has “His bowstring.” The meaning is uncertain.
“A brood” renders a rare word, and the meaning is uncertain.
“Not a helper belongs to them” is rendered “No one restrains them”; the meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Dignity” is rendered “honor.”
“My life pours itself out on me” is rendered “my soul is poured out within me.”
NASB has “it” where the Hebrew may mean “he.”
“Disguises itself” is rendered “is distorted”; the meaning of the verse is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Considered carefully in me” is rendered “turn Your attention against me.”
“Hostile” is rendered “persecute.”
The written text reads “success,” the reading aloud “storm”; NASB follows the reading aloud.
“A house of appointed meeting” is rendered “the house of meeting.”
The Hebrew is difficult; NASB renders it as a question, and the meaning is uncertain.
“The hard of day” is rendered “the one whose life is hard.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Inward parts” is rendered “I am … within,” and “not been still” as “cannot relax.”
“Being dark … with not sun” is rendered “mourning without comfort”; the meaning is uncertain.
“Daughters of an ostrich” is rendered “ostriches.”
“From heat” is rendered “with fever.”
